sunil.kumar: Hey team — after rotating our service API key via Vault this morning, our webhook workers started returning 401s to Redwood API. Affected all pods across 3 clusters. Quick curl test and error below.

sunil.kumar: ```
curl -v https://api.redwoodai.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_oldkey123" \n  -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
* Server returned 401: {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```

maria.support: Thanks — can you paste a request_id from the logs and the approximate time this started? Also did the rotation use a versioned secret or a full replace? Any proxies or edge workers in front?

sunil.kumar: Request id from one failing call: req_01GfXq9a0tN7eP. Started around 09:12 UTC. We rotated by creating a new version in Vault and updating the secret reference; our sidecar (secrets-refresher) should hot-swap env vars. No external proxy besides company edge.

alex.eng-oncall: Quick gut check: 401 invalid_api_key usually means the server saw the key we presented as unknown/expired. Two common causes: 1) some processes still running with the old key in env/volume and never reloaded, or 2) header formatting got mangled by a proxy/sidecar. Can you exec into one of the failing pods and verify the env var?

sunil.kumar: Ran `kubectl exec -it webhook-worker-5 -- printenv | grep REDWOOD_API_KEY` — shows `REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_oldkey123`. Our refresher logged that it wrote the new secret but then: ```
secrets-refresher[1]: 2026-03-17T09:11:58Z wrote secret version v2 to /etc/secrets/redwood_key
secrets-refresher[1]: 2026-03-17T09:11:58Z notifying process pid 2345 to reload
secrets-refresher[1]: 2026-03-17T09:11:58Z reload command returned 0
app[2345]: WARNING: reloaded config but REDWOOD_API_KEY unchanged (source: env)
```

maria.support: That log line is the clue — the refresher wrote the file but the app reads the key from env at process start. Many apps don't re-read env after start. Workarounds: 1) restart the deployment (kubectl rollout restart), 2) change app to read secret file (mounted) instead of env, or 3) have the refresher restart the process. Can you try a restart on one pod and retry the request id?

sunil.kumar: We tried a rolling restart earlier and saw the same 401s for a subset of pods — turns out our CI had pinned an older ReplicaSet so some pods didn't rotate. After forcing a full rollout and verifying all pods show new image + env, retry curl for the same pod returned 200.

alex.eng-oncall: Another note — if you have long-lived connections (gRPC/keep-alive) in front of the API, some clients will reuse the same connection and metadata. If the server invalidates a key mid-connection, some SDKs may not surface a fresh token and continue to send the old key. In that case you need to restart the process or reconnect.

sunil.kumar: Ah — we do have a persistent gRPC stream from the worker to our aggregator. Those streams showed the old auth metadata until we restarted the worker; after restart all streams reconnected with the new key and errors stopped.

maria.support: For records: the server logs for req_01GfXq9a0tN7eP show `invalid_api_key` at 2026-03-17T09:12:05Z and the audit entry lists the submitted key as `sk_live_oldkey123` (key revoked at rotation). Action items: ensure refresher either restarts process or writes to a file that the app reads without relying on env, add a post-rotate hook to force reconnects for long-lived clients, and add monitoring alert for sudden 401 spikes.

sunil.kumar: Thanks — that checklist is exactly what fixed it. Rolling restart + forcing sidecar to restart worker processes cleared the errors. We'll switch to file-mounted secret access in the next deploy.

maria.support: Great — marking this as resolved. If you want, DM me the audit IDs and we'll attach them to the support ticket for postmortem. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: support ticket #2026-413 closed by maria.support (resolution: restart/rotate propagation).
